research.instructionsPreview:
Zen MCP drives an owned Zen Browser; it never attaches to an existing session. Spaces are workspaces, and reads never change focus.
Orient with zen_status, zen_spaces_list, zen_tabs_list, and search before opening: zen_find_text, zen_search

tools.name: zen_read_page
tools.firstParagraph: Extract one tab, including tabs in other spaces, without focusing. Use snapshot for a bounded value-free control view with refs, outline, text preview and completeness flags; semantic for landmarks, repeated structures, forms, dialogs and a confidence-labelled page type. Use markdown for prose, links for sources, tables for data; `selector` narrows scope and text is paged with offset/nextOffset.

tools.name: zen_show_evidence_batch
tools.firstParagraph: Verify up to 20 citations, five per source, two at a time. Sources are grouped, tabs reused or opened once in the background, and each citation returns its own result. One non-http(s) URL rejects the batch before anything opens.

tools.name: zen_search_tabs
tools.firstParagraph: Find literal text across up to 30 open tabs and report which contain it, with offsets and excerpts. Read-only. Narrow with `space` or `tab_ids`; per-tab failures are reported without failing the batch.

tools.name: zen_show_evidence
tools.firstParagraph: Verify an exact quote in a source, scroll to it, and mark it; reuses an open matching tab or opens the source in the background. Count it as supported only when ok and verified are true. focus=true is visible.

tools.name: zen_status
tools.firstParagraph: Report the connected Zen Browser, its version, active space and tab, and every space with tab and folder counts. Use it first to orient yourself; a successful call proves the bridge is live.

tools.name: zen_events
tools.firstParagraph: Collect events after a cursor: Stop, Pause, Resume, watches, questions, plus observed tab, navigation, document and dialog transitions. `waitSeconds` long-polls up to 25. `missed` counts evicted events and `filtered` counts allowlist drops. Transitions are evidence, not cause. A stop means stop; a pause means stop retrying browser tools until resume.

tools.name: zen_config
tools.firstParagraph: Show effective policy and storage: read-only, allowlist, audit, data directory, surface, launch settings, pause, and consent. Use it to explain a blocked call; it needs no browser.

tools.name: zen_tabs_open
tools.firstParagraph: Open up to 30 URLs in a space without changing what the user sees (background defaults true). Returns the new tabs with ids. Split longer lists. Optionally use an existing folder or a Firefox container.

tools.name: zen_tabs_list
tools.firstParagraph: List open tabs across spaces in the window, including inactive ones, with ids, titles, URLs, space, folder, and state. Filter by space, title or URL substring, or pinned/folder state. Ids are valid only while the tab stays open.

tools.name: zen_read_pages
tools.firstParagraph: Read up to 10 tabs in one call, three at a time. Each tab succeeds or fails independently. One format, selector, and offset apply to the batch; use it for the first pass across sources, then read selectively.

tools.name: zen_tools_search
tools.firstParagraph: Search Zen MCP's full capability catalogue by keyword or category, including tools not currently exposed. Pass `name` to get one tool's description and input schema. Use it before zen_tools_use.

tools.name: zen_find_text
tools.firstParagraph: Find literal text in one tab and return match offsets with short excerpts. Read-only: no selection, scroll, or highlight. Case and typographic folding by default; the query is text, not a regex.

tools.name: zen_progress
tools.firstParagraph: Show or update a persistent progress card with a Stop button. Call at each stage of long work; `done:true` hides it and acknowledges Stop. Poll zen_events to notice Stop.

tools.name: zen_space_create
tools.firstParagraph: Create a space for a job. It does not switch by default, so the user stays put. Name it descriptively; use switchTo only when the user asked to go there.

tools.name: zen_notify
tools.firstParagraph: Show a small activity card in Zen. With `space`, it gets a button that takes the user there, which is the handover for a finished background job.

tools.name: zen_spaces_list
tools.firstParagraph: List every Zen space with its id, name, icon, and tab, pinned, and folder counts. Space ids and names are accepted wherever a tool takes a space.

tools.name: zen_tools_use
tools.firstParagraph: Invoke any Zen MCP tool by name, including one not in the current surface, with normal validation, policy, audit, and result shape. Set publish=true to add it to tools/list when the client supports list changes.

core.instructionsPreview:
Zen MCP drives an owned Zen Browser; it never attaches to an existing session. Spaces are workspaces, and reads never change focus.

Use markdown for prose, links for sources, tables for data; `selector` narrows scope and text is paged with offset/nextOffset.

tools.name: zen_type
tools.firstParagraph: Type into one field by ref, semantic `target` (label, placeholder, role+name, text, or selector), or top-level CSS selector. `clear` replaces; the default appends. `observed` says whether the field matched without returning the value or length; sensitive fields are not read back. File inputs are refused. `effect.delta` reports observed changes.

tools.name: zen_click
tools.firstParagraph: Click one control by ref, semantic `target` (role+name, text, label, placeholder, or selector), or top-level CSS selector. One resolver re-validates before input; two matches fail with candidates. Use only when asked. Refs expire with the next read; removed or navigated nodes return element_not_found. Real input can submit, navigate, or purchase. `effect.delta` reports observed changes, not proof.

tools.name: zen_wait_for
tools.firstParagraph: Wait for exactly one condition in a tab: selector present, visible or enabled, text, URL substring, title substring, a document change or identity, a new tab, a tab closing, or a dialog appearing. Read-only. Timeout returns matched:false, not an error.

tools.name: zen_launch
tools.firstParagraph: Start a Zen window owned by Zen MCP, prove ownership, lock down Marionette, and attach the bridge. Shows a one-time approval card. Use only when a tool reports Zen unreachable or after the owned session was lost; it never attaches to an existing browser.

tools.name: zen_tab_select
tools.firstParagraph: Bring a tab into view, switching space and possibly focusing the window. This takes over the user's screen; use zen_read_page for background reading instead.

tools.name: zen_answers
tools.firstParagraph: List questions still open in Zen and recently answered ones. Use it after zen_ask returns pending or deferred, or to collect a late reply.

tools.name: zen_space_create
tools.firstParagraph: Create a space for a job. It does not switch by default, so the user stays put. Name it descriptively; use switchTo only when the user asked to go there.

tools.name: zen_folder_create
tools.firstParagraph: Create a Zen folder around existing tabs, optionally collapsed. Tabs must share one space and must not already be grouped or split. Up to 100 tabs.

tools.name: zen_notify
tools.firstParagraph: Show a small activity card in Zen. With `space`, it gets a button that takes the user there, which is the handover for a finished background job.

tools.name: zen_folder_add_tabs
tools.firstParagraph: Move existing tabs into an existing folder. Tabs must be in the folder's space and not already grouped.

tools.name: zen_tabs_group
tools.firstParagraph: Create one Zen folder per domain for ungrouped, unpinned tabs in a space. Leaves pinned tabs, essentials, and existing folders alone. Run it once per space.

tools.name: zen_glance
tools.firstParagraph: Open Zen's Glance overlay for a URL or an open tab without creating a tab. Visible on the current page; use when the user wants a quick look, not a full switch.

tools.name: zen_spaces_list
tools.firstParagraph: List every Zen space with its id, name, icon, and tab, pinned, and folder counts. Space ids and names are accepted wherever a tool takes a space.

tools.name: zen_split_view
tools.firstParagraph: Show 2 to 4 tabs from the active space side by side. This changes what the user sees; use it only when asked or for a comparison they requested.

tools.name: zen_space_switch
tools.firstParagraph: Switch the browser to an existing space by id or name. This changes what the user sees, so do it only when asked or after telling them.

tools.name: zen_tools_use
tools.firstParagraph: Invoke any Zen MCP tool by name, including one not in the current surface, with normal validation, policy, audit, and result shape. Set publish=true to add it to tools/list when the client supports list changes.

tools.name: zen_essentials
tools.firstParagraph: Add or remove essentials, which stay pinned above every space. Removing also unpins. Up to 20 tabs; use sparingly and never on user tabs without asking.

tools.name: zen_clear_evidence
tools.firstParagraph: Remove highlight overlays created by this bridge session, for one tab or all marked tabs. Page-owned nodes are never touched.

tools.name: zen_folders_list
tools.firstParagraph: List tab folders in the window with their space, label, collapsed state, and tab ids.

tools.name: zen_tabs_close
tools.firstParagraph: Close tabs by id, up to 100. Destructive to the user's session: close only tabs you opened or tabs the user explicitly named.

tools.name: zen_containers_list
tools.firstParagraph: List the Firefox containers in this profile. Pass a container name or id to zen_tabs_open or zen_glance to isolate a site.

tools.name: zen_pin_tabs
tools.firstParagraph: Pin tabs to the space's pinned strip, or unpin them. Essentials use zen_essentials instead.

tools.name: zen_split_close
tools.firstParagraph: Unsplit the group containing a tab, or the current split view. Tabs stay open.

tools.name: zen_session_delete
